title: Overnight Sourdough Pizza Dough
equipment: 4-litre tub or large bowl, for the dough

scenes.title: Overnight sourdough pizza dough
scenes.vo: Overnight sourdough pizza dough. It makes four dough balls of about 280 grams, each one a pizza about 30 centimetres across.
scenes.voUS: Overnight sourdough pizza dough. It makes four dough balls of about 10 ounces, each one a pizza about 12 inches across.
cap: Four pizzas, one overnight rise. Start the morning before you want to eat.
capUS: Four pizzas, one overnight rise. Start the morning before you want to eat.

scenes.title: What you need
scenes.vo: Here's what you need. To feed the starter: 40 grams of active starter, 80 grams of strong white flour, and 80 grams of water at about 27 degrees Celsius. For the dough: 600 grams of 00 or strong white flour, 390 grams of water at about 27 degrees, 120 grams of the levain you made that morning, and 15 grams of fine sea salt. You'll also need a little olive oil for the container, and flour for dusting. Choose unfortified flour, with no added folic acid. Small mills sell it.
scenes.voUS: Here's what you need. To feed the starter: 3 tablespoons of active starter, two-thirds of a cup of bread flour, and a third of a cup of water at about 80 degrees Fahrenheit. For the dough: four and three-quarter cups of 00 or bread flour, one and two-thirds cups of water at about 80 degrees, half a cup of the levain you made that morning, and two and a half teaspoons of fine sea salt. You'll also need a little olive oil for the container, and flour for dusting. Choose unfortified flour, with no added folic acid. Small mills sell it.
cap: Ingredients for four 280 g dough balls.
Use unfortified flour, with no added folic acid. Small mills sell it.
capUS: Ingredients for four 10 oz dough balls.
Use unfortified flour, with no added folic acid. Small mills sell it.

scenes.vo: At about 6 in the evening, start the dough. In your tub, combine 600 grams of flour with 390 grams of water at about 27 degrees Celsius. Mix just until no dry flour is left. Cover, and rest for 30 minutes.

Mix just until no dry flour is left. Cover and rest 30 minutes.

scenes.title: Mix by hand
scenes.vo: With a wet hand, fold the dough over onto itself, then squeeze it through between your thumb and fingers. Keep folding and squeezing for 3 to 5 minutes, until you can't feel any grains of salt or streaks of levain. The mixed dough should be about 24 degrees Celsius.
scenes.voUS: With a wet hand, fold the dough over onto itself, then squeeze it through between your thumb and fingers. Keep folding and squeezing for 3 to 5 minutes, until you can't feel any grains of salt or streaks of levain. The mixed dough should be about 75 degrees Fahrenheit.
cap: With a wet hand, fold the dough over onto itself.
Squeeze it through between thumb and fingers, then fold again, for 3 to 5 minutes.
The mixed dough should be about 24 °C.
capUS: With a wet hand, fold the dough over onto itself.
Squeeze it through between thumb and fingers, then fold again, for 3 to 5 minutes.
The mixed dough should be about 75 °F.

scenes.title: Stretch and fold
scenes.vo: Over the next hour and a half, give the dough three sets of stretch-and-folds, 30 minutes apart. Lift one side, stretch it up, and fold it across. Turn the tub and repeat, until you've gone all the way round.
scenes.voUS: Over the next hour and a half, give the dough three sets of stretch-and-folds, 30 minutes apart. Lift one side, stretch it up, and fold it across. Turn the tub and repeat, until you've gone all the way round.

scenes.title: Rise overnight
scenes.vo: Cover it and leave it overnight, at around 20 degrees Celsius, for 10 to 12 hours. It's ready when it has risen by half to three-quarters, with bubbles on the top and at the sides.
scenes.voUS: Cover it and leave it overnight, at around 68 degrees Fahrenheit, for 10 to 12 hours. It's ready when it has risen by half to three-quarters, with bubbles on the top and at the sides.

It is ready when it has risen by half to three-quarters, with bubbles on top.

scenes.vo: At about 7 the next morning, lightly flour your work surface and tip the dough out onto it. Using your scraper, cut it into four pieces of about 280 grams each.

scenes.title: Refrigerate
scenes.vo: Put the balls in a lightly oiled, lidded container, with room to grow, and refrigerate. They're ready to use after 6 hours, and keep for up to 3 days. Take them out 1 to 2 hours before you bake.

scenes.title: The schedule
scenes.vo: So the schedule is: feed the starter at 10 in the morning, mix the dough at 6 in the evening, and shape the balls at 7 the next morning. The dough is ready from 1 in the afternoon, and keeps in the fridge for up to 3 days.
